nodes.title: People
nodes.detail: Only people decide scope, rule changes, architecture and the H&M licence question (OI-5). They also tick the preconditions an agent cannot: local commits, the committed spec and the branch model, and the accounts and secrets (Supabase, Vercel, GitHub, SMTP, artifact location, worker host). Agents propose; they never decide these and never create an account or enter a key.

nodes.title: Sources and rules
nodes.detail: Requirements come from the four documents; the checkers read them too. The datasets never leave their folder (BR-59); absolute paths for the datasets, team photos, the one H&M cache and the artifact folder are SPARTA_DATA_ROOT_HM, SPARTA_DATA_ROOT_MNIST, SPARTA_TEAM_PHOTOS, SPARTA_HM_CACHE and SPARTA_ARTIFACT_DIR in the git-ignored workflow/local.env. Standing rules: stay in the project, no Claude trailer, time-box investigations, outward actions need a yes.

nodes.title: Orchestration
nodes.detail: The orchestrator never writes feature code and never approves G1. The spec agent turns requirements into work orders with runnable acceptance checks. STATE.md is the only memory between sessions. The orchestrator merges work-order branches into the release's integration branch and checks usage before and after every work order. It arms a one-shot resume (the trigger) before each work order, for two minutes after the 5-hour reset; at 85% of that window it writes the checkpoint and stops; at 90% of any weekly window, or when usage cannot be read, it stops and waits for the owner. It refreshes STATE.md every 15 minutes while it runs.

nodes.title: Consultants
nodes.detail: Consultants write short memos that cite the documents. They cannot edit files, cannot approve, and do not replace the style specialist, the SA or a lawyer.

nodes.title: Design
nodes.detail: User-facing work orders only. The brief comes first; the visual craft agent builds presentational components and tokens to it (components/ui and styles only) and the frontend maker builds the pages; the critic scores them. A score below the bar goes back to the visual agent.

nodes.title: Build: makers
chips: BRD to LLD stay in step
nodes.detail: One maker per work order, in an isolated worktree. Makers never edit the same files, never edit gate scripts, never commit an H&M-trained file and never judge their own work. A path-to-owner table gives every path one owner, and a G2 script fails a diff outside the work order's In-scope list. Accounts and keys are never theirs.

nodes.title: Check: checkers
nodes.detail: Scripts run first (the scope and ownership script included); red goes straight back to the maker. The gate engineer writes the scripts and the CI workflows outside every maker's scope and Spec QC reviews them. G4 keeps the H&M-trained files marked not yet built in the manifest on main and on every release and work-order branch until G7 (manifest_check enforces it). Spec QC judges against the spec on the base branch and approves G1. A checker may only fail work by citing a script result or a quoted line of the specification. Two fix loops at most, then the orchestrator decides.

nodes.title: Demo and approve
nodes.detail: The demo agent drives the running app through the release's acceptance script (R0 and R1 are shown as a recorded test run). It never shows anything that has not run. The Opus approver reads all evidence. The product owner gives the final yes; merging to main and tagging are theirs.

nodes.title: Retro and improve
chips: Opus: gate G8, not the retro
nodes.detail: After every release. The retro proposes changes to the workflow; the editor applies them on a branch; the workflow approver, a different agent from the retro agent, approves or rejects each one (G8) before it counts.

releases: Learned layer and the standout feature
gates: Gates: G1 ready (Spec QC, owner; accounts ticked) | G2 scripts (CI runs, orchestrator blocks; scope check) | G2b review | G3 spec | G4 privacy and licence (H&M-trained files marked not built on main and release branches) | G5 design

G6 release (Opus, then the owner) | G7 licence (people; blocks pinning the H&M files on main or in a pilot build) | G8 workflow change (workflow approver) | G9 style review (style specialist, R3 and R4)
g7: G7: a person closes the H&M licence check before the H&M-trained files are pinned on main or any learned part is switched on in a pilot or production build
